meaning: A small device you carried that beeped when someone wanted to reach you. Its screen showed a number to call back.
clues: It helped people get a message when they were away from home.
You wore it on your belt or kept it in a pocket.
It beeped, and a small screen showed the number to call back.
Before cell phones were common, many people carried one to stay in touch with work or home.
It has five letters and starts with P. Another name for it is a beeper.
assumes: An answering machine stays at home and records messages
A payphone is a public phone you put coins in

decoys.meaning: A machine that answers the phone when you are away and records a message from the caller.
A public phone that you used by putting in coins or using a card.
A machine that scans a paper page and sends a copy over a phone line. Another machine prints the copy.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, a beep on your belt meant someone wanted you. Then you ran for the nearest payphone.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: a text message on your phone. You can reply right where you are, with no payphone hunt.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Hunting for a payphone with a pocket full of coins was practically a sport.

sources.name: Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Motorola BPR2000 Pager
